newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lazard Freres tops 1996 French M&A rankings.
newsitem.headline: Lazard Freres tops 1996 French M&A rankings.

text.p: French investment bank Lazard Freres topped the 1996 French mergers and acquisitions ranking by Fusions & Acquisitions Magazine, while other banks also saw big increases in their merger and acquisition income.

The magazine said on Tuesday that while Lazard's was for long the sole bank to advise on deals totalling over 50 billion francs a year, no less than seven banks did so in 1996, of which five were French and two American.
Last week, the Capital Finance newsletter said Goldman Sachs had dethroned Lazard Freres, but in the Fusions & Acquisitions ranking Goldman Sachs came in third.

In 1996, the French merger and acquisition scene was dominated by the merger between insurers AXA and UAP, the successful raid on Docks de France by privately-held Auchan and the sale of Poliet by Saint-Gobain.

The paper said that 1997 also looked set to be a good year for the sector with a France Telecom stake sale, the Thomson-CSF privatisation, the merger of Aerospatiale and Dassault Aviation and other deals.

The magazine said that 1996 had also seen records in commission income and end-of-year bonuses, with the best performing banks commanding fees of between 100 to 500 million francs. The publication said that fee income remained a taboo subject for French financial institutions.
"In the slipstream of the U.S. and British markets which have hit their historic highs in 1996, the French market has likely also beaten its previous historic record of 1990," the monthly said.
